items.description:
Quetta Gladiators have dismissed speculation about a possible sale of the franchise or an exit from the Pakistan Super League (PSL), reaffirming their financial stability and commitment to the competition.
In a statement issued on Friday, the franchise said rumours circulating on social media and in some media reports had been “taken out of context, misconstrued or were entirely without foundation”.

items.title: Fleeing murder suspect crashes into elephant in Sri Lanka
items.description:
A Sri Lankan man suspected of fatally stabbing a woman was arrested on Friday after he crashed his scooter into a wild elephant as he attempted to escape, police said.
The 49-year-old man is accused of stabbing the woman in her home in the northern district of Anuradhapura, a police official told AFP.
However, his attempted escape ended when his scooter crashed into the elephant as it emerged from the jungle onto the road a short distance away, the official said.
Witnesses told police the elephant appeared to be unharmed and retreated into the jungle.

items.title: ECP says it cannot force parties to field women on winnable seats
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday made it clear that the allocation of party tickets was an internal matter for political parties and that it had no legal authority to intervene.
The ECP explained its position a day after a National Assembly panel directed it to ensure that the five per cent quota for women on general seats under Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, is implemented in a manner that women are fielded on seats where their victory is certain.
